newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow markedly on jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow markedly on jobs.

text.p: Australian bond spreads narrowed markedly on Thursday, and the curve steepened sharply, after local bonds rallied on weaker than expected employment data for March.
Employment fell by 33,900 in March, of which 30,400 were full-time jobs, against median forecasts of a 13,500 rise. The unemployment rate of 8.7 percent was in line with expectations.
The data reinforced to the markets that there was no need for Australia to follow the U.S. lead and start lifting interest rates, and for some it even left open the chance of a rate cut.
"The employment data is positive for Australian bond market sentiment, but more particularly in keeping the yield curve on a steepening trend," UBS Australia chief economist Steve Roberts said.

Analysts said bonds should remain well positioned for further spread narrowings, with both first quarter inflation data due later this month and the Federal budget next month both expected to be positives for the market.
At the short end, expectations of constant local rates, and the glimmer of a possible rate cut, saw spreads to U.S. three year Treasuries narrow to under 30 points, before closing at 35 points.
The close was the lowest in the spread's recent history, and well down of the spreads of 250 points at this time last year.
Spreads to U.S. 10-year Treasuries narrowed to close at their smallest margin since mid-February, when the market began factoring out expectations of a fourth cut in official rates.
While the spread closed at 107 points, soon after the data it had edged towards 100 basis points, a level which is expected to prove tough to break through.
With the short end leading the way, both the futures and physical curves steepened markedly.

The futures curve closed at its steepest since the June contracts became active last month, while the physicals curve was just above Monday's 103 point close. The physical yield spread has not closed above 105 points since September 1995.
